et budget.explanation: "Et budget" means "a budget", a plan for what money comes in and goes out. To stay within it, say "at overholde budgettet" (to stick to the budget).

sentence.da: Vi har et lille **budget** til ferien.
sentence.en: We have a small budget for the vacation.

et budskab.explanation: "Et budskab" means "a message", the main thing someone wants you to understand, in a speech, a film or an ad. For a message you send to someone, such as a text, Danes use "en besked" (a message).

sentence.da: Filmens **budskab** er, at venskab er vigtigere end penge.
sentence.en: The film's message is that friendship is more important than money.

et bur.explanation: "Et bur" means "a cage", an enclosure with bars for keeping animals such as birds, hamsters or rabbits.

sentence.da: Fuglen sidder i et **bur** med tremmer af metal.
sentence.en: The bird sits in a cage with metal bars.

et bureau.explanation: "Et bureau" means "an agency" or "an office", often in a compound: "et rejsebureau" (a travel agency). It also means a dresser: "Tøjet ligger i bureauet" (The clothes are in the dresser).

sentence.da: Et **bureau** hjælper kunder med at planlægge rejser eller reklamer.
sentence.en: An agency helps customers plan trips or advertising.

et busstoppested.explanation: "Et busstoppested" means "a bus stop". It is made from bus (bus) and stoppested (a place where something stops). People often shorten it to "et stoppested" (a stop).

sentence.da: Jeg venter på bussen ved et **busstoppested**.
sentence.en: I am waiting for the bus at a bus stop.

et byggemarked.explanation: "Et byggemarked" means "a DIY store", a big store that sells building materials, garden supplies and things for home repairs to people who do the work themselves.

sentence.da: I et **byggemarked** kan du købe brædder, skruer og maling.
sentence.en: In a DIY store you can buy boards, screws and paint.

et byggeri.explanation: "Et byggeri" means "a construction", the work of building or a whole building project. It also names the building industry: "Hun arbejder i byggeriet" (She works in construction).

sentence.da: Et **byggeri** af et nyt hus tager ofte mange måneder.
sentence.en: Building a new house often takes many months.

et bytte.explanation: "Et bytte" means "prey", an animal that another animal hunts. It is spelled like the verb "at bytte" (to swap), so it also means an exchange: "Det var et godt bytte" (That was a good swap).

sentence.da: Ørnen styrter ned mod sit **bytte** i marken.
sentence.en: The eagle dives down toward its prey in the field.

et bål.explanation: "Et bål" means "a bonfire" or "a campfire", an open fire outdoors. A fire that destroys things is "en brand" (a fire): "Der er brand i huset" (The house is on fire).

sentence.da: Vi sidder rundt om et **bål** og griller pølser.
sentence.en: We sit around a bonfire and grill sausages.

et bånd.explanation: "Et bånd" means "a ribbon", a long, narrow strip of fabric for tying or decorating things. It also means "tape" for recording, and between people it means "a bond": "et stærkt bånd mellem søstre" (a strong bond between sisters).

sentence.da: Hun binder et rødt **bånd** om gaven.
sentence.en: She ties a red ribbon around the gift.

et bælt.explanation: "Et bælt" means "a strait", a narrow stretch of water between two pieces of land. Denmark has two famous ones: "Storebælt" (the Great Belt) and "Lillebælt" (the Little Belt). A belt for trousers is spelled with an extra e: "et bælte" (a belt).

sentence.da: Vandet mellem Fyn og Sjælland er et **bælt**.
sentence.en: The water between Funen and Zealand is a strait.

et bælte.explanation: "Et bælte" means "a belt", a strap you wear around your waist, usually to hold up trousers. "Et sikkerhedsbælte" (a seat belt) is built on the same word, from sikkerhed (safety).

sentence.da: Et **bælte** holder bukserne oppe.
sentence.en: A belt holds the trousers up.

et bær.explanation: "Et bær" means "a berry". Many berry names end in "bær": "jordbær" (strawberry) and "blåbær" (blueberry).

sentence.da: Et **bær** vokser på en busk og er ofte sødt.
sentence.en: A berry grows on a bush and is often sweet.

et bæst.explanation: "Et bæst" means "a beast", a big, wild and frightening creature. It is also used about a rough, unpleasant person: "Han er et bæst" (He is a brute).

sentence.da: Et stort **bæst** med skarpe tænder gemte sig i skoven.
sentence.en: A big beast with sharp teeth hid in the forest.

et børneværelse.explanation: "Et børneværelse" means "a children's room", the room in a home where the kids sleep and play. It is built from børn (children) and værelse (room). The start "børne-" is also in "en børnebog" (a children's book).

sentence.da: Der er mange bamser i vores **børneværelse**.
sentence.en: There are many teddy bears in our children's room.

at censurere.explanation: "At censurere" means "to censor", to cut or forbid parts of a text or a film so that people cannot see them. Do not mix it up with "en censor" (an examiner), the outside person who helps grade a school exam.

sentence.da: Nogle lande vil **censurere** nyhederne, så folk ikke får hele sandheden.
sentence.en: Some countries want to censor the news so people do not get the whole truth.

at checke ind.explanation: "At checke ind" means "to check in", whether at a hotel or at an airport. The check-in itself is called "et check-in" (a check-in).

sentence.da: Vi kan **checke ind** på hotellet klokken to.
sentence.en: We can check in at the hotel at two o'clock.

at checke ud.explanation: "At checke ud" means "to check out", to leave a hotel at the end of your stay. The opposite is "at checke ind" (to check in).

sentence.da: Vi skal **checke ud** af hotellet i dag.
sentence.en: We have to check out of the hotel today.

at cirkulere.explanation: "At cirkulere" means "to circulate", to move around in a loop or from person to person. Use it for something that keeps going around: "Blodet cirkulerer rundt i kroppen" (Blood circulates around the body), "Pengene cirkulerer i byen" (The money circulates in the town).

sentence.da: Rygter kan **cirkulere** hurtigt på en lille arbejdsplads.
sentence.en: Rumors can circulate quickly at a small workplace.

at citere.explanation: "At citere" means "to quote", to repeat the exact words of a person or a text. To name the speech or text the words come from, add "fra" (from): "Han citerer fra en tale" (He quotes from a speech).

sentence.da: Man må gerne **citere** en bog, hvis man nævner forfatteren.
sentence.en: You may quote a book if you mention the author.

at cykle.explanation: "At cykle" means "to cycle" or "to ride a bike". It comes from "en cykel" (a bicycle). To say where you are cycling to, add "til" (to): "Jeg cykler til skole" (I cycle to school).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **cykle** på arbejde.
sentence.en: I want to cycle to work.

central.explanation: "Central" means "central", in the middle of a place. It is also used for the most important part of something: "den centrale idé" (the main idea).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en **central** lejlighed tæt på stationen.
sentence.en: We live in a central apartment close to the station.

champagne.explanation: "Champagne" means "champagne", a bubbly wine for celebrations. Only bubbly wine from the Champagne region of France carries this name.

sentence.da: Til nytår drikker vi **champagne** og skåler.
sentence.en: At New Year's we drink champagne and toast.

charme.explanation: "Charme" means "charm", the pleasant quality that makes people like someone. It can also describe a place: "en hytte med charme" (a cottage with charm).

sentence.da: Han har meget **charme**, og alle kan lide ham.
sentence.en: He has a lot of charm, and everyone likes him.

charmerende.explanation: "Charmerende" means "charming" and describes someone who wins people over easily. It is also used for places: "en charmerende by" (a charming town).

sentence.da: Han er **charmerende** og får alle til at smile.
sentence.en: He is charming and makes everyone smile.

chili.explanation: "En chili" means "a chili", the small fruit that burns in your mouth and adds heat to food.

sentence.da: **Chili** er lille og meget stærk.
sentence.en: Chili is small and very hot.

chips.explanation: "Chips" means "potato chips" (called crisps in British English). To name a portion, use "en pose chips" (a bag of chips). Do not mix it up with "pommes frites" (French fries).

sentence.da: **Chips** er lavet af kartofler og smager salt.
sentence.en: Chips are made of potatoes and taste salty.

chokerende.explanation: "Chokerende" means "shocking", so upsetting or unexpected that it hits you hard. Do not mix it up with "chokeret" (shocked): "chokerende" names what causes the feeling ("en chokerende nyhed", a shocking piece of news), while "chokeret" says how you feel ("Jeg er chokeret", I am shocked).

sentence.da: Nyheden var **chokerende**, og alle blev helt stille.
sentence.en: The news was shocking, and everyone went completely quiet.

chokeret.explanation: "Chokeret" means "shocked", how you feel when something bad surprises you. What causes the feeling is "chokerende" (shocking).

sentence.da: Jeg blev **chokeret**, da jeg hørte nyheden.
sentence.en: I was shocked when I heard the news.

chokolade.explanation: "Chokolade" means "chocolate". It is also the drink, as in "en varm chokolade" (a hot chocolate). The "ch" at the start is said like "sh".

sentence.da: **Chokolade** er sød og brun.
sentence.en: Chocolate is sweet and brown.

cirka.explanation: "Cirka" means "approximately" or "about", used before a number, time or amount that is not exact. In writing, it is shortened to "ca."

sentence.da: Det er **cirka** tre kilometer.
sentence.en: It is about three kilometers.

civil.explanation: "Civil" means "civilian" and "civil", for people and things that are not part of the army. It is also the word in "civil ulydighed" (civil disobedience), where people break a rule on purpose to protest, without violence.

sentence.da: Soldaten tog uniformen af og gik rundt i **civil**.
sentence.en: The soldier took off the uniform and walked around in plain clothes.

co2.explanation: "CO2" means "carbon dioxide", the gas released when we burn fuel such as coal, oil and gas, and when we breathe out. Too much of it in the air makes the planet warmer. The full Danish word is "kuldioxid" (carbon dioxide).

sentence.da: Når vi kører bil, udleder vi **CO2** til luften.
sentence.en: When we drive a car, we release CO2 into the air.

cornflakes.explanation: "Cornflakes" means "cornflakes", the breakfast cereal. To name a portion, use "en skål cornflakes" (a bowl of cornflakes).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser **cornflakes** med mælk til morgenmad.
sentence.en: I eat cornflakes with milk for breakfast.

couscous.explanation: "Couscous" means "couscous", tiny round grains made from wheat and served as a side dish.

sentence.da: Jeg hælder varmt vand over **couscous**.
sentence.en: I pour hot water over couscous.

creme.explanation: "En creme" means "cream" for your skin, for example for dry skin or after the sun. For cream in coffee or cooking, say "fløde" (cream) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg smører **creme** på mine hænder.
sentence.en: I rub cream on my hands.

creme fraiche.explanation: "Creme fraiche" means "crème fraîche", a thick, slightly sour cream. You stir it into sauces and soups: "Jeg putter creme fraiche i suppen" (I put crème fraîche in the soup).

sentence.da: Jeg putter **creme fraiche** på min bagte kartoffel.
sentence.en: I put crème fraîche on my baked potato.

cykling.explanation: "Cykling" means "cycling" as an activity or sport: "Cykling er sundt" (Cycling is healthy). To state that you are riding a bike right now, use "at cykle" (to cycle): "Jeg cykler" (I am cycling).

sentence.da: Jeg har en cykel og elsker **cykling**.
sentence.en: I have a bicycle and love cycling.

en café.explanation: "En café" means "a café", a place for coffee, cake or a light meal. For a sit-down dinner with a full menu, Danes usually say "en restaurant" (a restaurant).

sentence.da: Vi drikker kaffe på en **café**.
sentence.en: We drink coffee at a café.

en campingplads.explanation: "En campingplads" means "a campsite". It is built from camping (camping) and plads (place), and "plads" also means "room": "Der er ikke plads her" (There is no room here).

sentence.da: På en **campingplads** kan man sove i telt.
sentence.en: On a campsite you can sleep in a tent.

en campus.explanation: "En campus" means "a campus", the area where the buildings of a school of higher education stand together, with a library and places to eat and study.

sentence.da: Mange studerende bor på eller tæt ved **campus**.
sentence.en: Many students live on or close to campus.

en cardigan.explanation: "En cardigan" means "a cardigan", a knitted top that opens down the front.

sentence.da: Hun tager en **cardigan** på, når det er køligt.
sentence.en: She puts on a cardigan when it is cool.

en carport.explanation: "En carport" means "a carport", a roof on posts where you park the car, with no walls: "Bilen holder i carporten" (The car is parked in the carport). A closed garage is "en garage" (a garage).

sentence.da: Vi parkerer bilen under vores **carport**.
sentence.en: We park the car under our carport.

en celle.explanation: "En celle" means "a cell" in three ways. In biology it is the smallest living part of a body. In a prison it is a small room for one prisoner. In a spreadsheet it is one box.

sentence.da: En **celle** er den mindste levende del af en krop.
sentence.en: A cell is the smallest living part of a body.

en censor.explanation: "En censor" means "an external examiner", a person from outside the school who joins an oral or written test and helps the school's own teacher decide the mark.

sentence.da: Til den mundtlige prøve sidder der både en lærer og en **censor**.
sentence.en: At the oral test, there is both a teacher and an external examiner.

en cent.explanation: "En cent" means "a cent", one hundredth of a euro or a dollar. Danish money is counted in "kroner" (the Danish currency) and "øre" (a hundredth of a krone) instead.

sentence.da: Den koster kun tyve **cent**.
sentence.en: It only costs twenty cents.

en centimeter.explanation: "En centimeter" means "a centimeter". Do not add an ending after a number: "ti centimeter" (ten centimeters).

sentence.da: Bordet er hundrede **centimeter** langt.
sentence.en: The table is a hundred centimeters long.

en ceremoni.explanation: "En ceremoni" means "a ceremony", a formal event that follows fixed steps, for example when people get married, graduate or receive a prize.

sentence.da: Ved en **ceremoni** gør man tingene på en fast, højtidelig måde.
sentence.en: At a ceremony you do things in a fixed, solemn way.

en champignon.explanation: "En champignon" means "a mushroom", the white kind you buy in a store.

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide **champignon** på pizza.
sentence.en: I like mushrooms on pizza.

en chance.explanation: "En chance" means "a chance" in two ways. It can be an opportunity: "Jeg fik en chance" (I got a chance). It can also be how likely something is: "Hun har en god chance" (She has a good chance).

sentence.da: Hun har en god **chance** for at vinde.
sentence.en: She has a good chance of winning.

en chauffør.explanation: "En chauffør" means "a driver", someone who drives as a job. For anyone driving their own car, use "en bilist" (a car driver).

sentence.da: Bussens **chauffør** hilser på alle.
sentence.en: The bus driver greets everyone.

en cheesecake.explanation: "En cheesecake" means "a cheesecake", a creamy cake made with soft cheese on a crumbly base.

sentence.da: **Cheesecake** laves af flødeost og æg.
sentence.en: Cheesecake is made of cream cheese and eggs.

en chef.explanation: "En chef" means "a boss" or "a manager". The ch sounds like English sh. For the head of a kitchen, Danish says "en køkkenchef" (a head chef).

sentence.da: Min **chef** bestemmer på kontoret.
sentence.en: My boss makes the decisions at the office.

en chokoladekage.explanation: "En chokoladekage" means "a chocolate cake". It is built from chokolade (chocolate) and kage (cake), and "kage" is also in "en gulerodskage" (a carrot cake) and "en ostekage" (a cheesecake).

sentence.da: En **chokoladekage** bages med kakao og smør.
sentence.en: A chocolate cake is baked with cocoa and butter.

en cigaret.explanation: "En cigaret" means "a cigarette". You smoke it with "at ryge" (to smoke): "Han ryger en cigaret" (He smokes a cigarette).

sentence.da: Han tænder en **cigaret** udenfor.
sentence.en: He lights a cigarette outside.

en cirkel.explanation: "En cirkel" means "a circle", a perfectly round flat shape. People also sit in one: "Vi sidder i en cirkel" (We sit in a circle). For a round 3D shape, use "en kugle" (a ball).

sentence.da: En **cirkel** er rund og har ingen hjørner.
sentence.en: A circle is round and has no corners.

en citron.explanation: "En citron" means "a lemon", a sour yellow fruit. The stress is on the last part: ci-TRON.

sentence.da: Kan jeg få en skive **citron** i teen?
sentence.en: Can I have a slice of lemon in the tea?

en coach.explanation: "En coach" means "a coach", someone who trains or guides a person or team. In sports, Danes also say "en træner" (a coach).

sentence.da: Vores **coach** hjælper os med at blive bedre.
sentence.en: Our coach helps us get better.

en computer.explanation: "En computer" means "a computer", spelled just like the English word. A laptop is "en bærbar computer" (a portable computer), often shortened to "en bærbar" (a portable one).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver en e-mail på min **computer**.
sentence.en: I am writing an email on my computer.

en computermus.explanation: "En computermus" means "a computer mouse", the device you click with. It is built from computer (computer) and mus (mouse), the same word as the animal.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke klikke, fordi min **computermus** er gået i stykker.
sentence.en: I cannot click because my computer mouse is broken.

en container.explanation: "En container" means "a container", usually a big metal box for waste or for shipping goods. For a small one for food, say "en beholder" (a food container).

sentence.da: De smider gammelt træ i en **container**.
sentence.en: They throw old wood in a container.

en croissant.explanation: "En croissant" means "a croissant", a flaky, buttery pastry in a curved shape.

sentence.da: Til morgenmad spiser jeg en **croissant** med smør.
sentence.en: For breakfast I eat a croissant with butter.

en cykel.explanation: "En cykel" means "a bicycle". Notice the spelling with y, not i. To say you go by bike, use "på cykel" (by bike) or "at tage cyklen" (to take the bike).

sentence.da: En **cykel** har to hjul.
sentence.en: A bicycle has two wheels.

en cykelhandler.explanation: "En cykelhandler" means "a bike dealer", a shop that sells and repairs bikes.

sentence.da: Jeg kan købe en ny cykel hos en **cykelhandler**.
sentence.en: I can buy a new bike at a bike dealer.

en cykelhjelm.explanation: "En cykelhjelm" means "a bike helmet", a hard cap you wear while riding. To say you are wearing one, use "have på" (have on): "Hun har cykelhjelm på" (She is wearing a bike helmet). To put it on, use "tage på" (put on): "Tag din cykelhjelm på" (Put on your bike helmet).

sentence.da: En **cykelhjelm** beskytter dit hoved.
sentence.en: A bike helmet protects your head.

en cykellås.explanation: "En cykellås" means "a bike lock". It is built from cykel (bike) and lås (lock). The same "lås" is in "en dørlås" (a door lock), and the verb is "at låse" (to lock).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger en **cykellås**, så ingen stjæler min cykel.
sentence.en: I use a bike lock so nobody steals my bike.

en cykelparkering.explanation: "En cykelparkering" means "a bike parking area", a place to leave your bike, often with racks.

sentence.da: Der er en stor **cykelparkering** foran stationen, og den er gratis.
sentence.en: There is a big bike parking area in front of the station, and it is free.

en cykelpumpe.explanation: "En cykelpumpe" means "a bike pump", used to fill a bike wheel with air. It is built from cykel (bike) and pumpe (pump).

sentence.da: Jeg pumper cyklen op med en **cykelpumpe**.
sentence.en: I pump up the bike with a bike pump.

en cykelsti.explanation: "En cykelsti" means "a bike lane", a path next to the road only for bikes. People on foot use "et fortov" (a sidewalk).

sentence.da: Der er en ny **cykelsti** langs vejen.
sentence.en: There is a new bike lane along the road.

en cykeltur.explanation: "En cykeltur" means "a bike ride". It is made from cykel (bicycle) and tur (trip). "Tur" also builds other words, such as "en biltur" (a car trip) and "en sejltur" (a boat trip).

sentence.da: Vi tager på **cykeltur** i skoven.
sentence.en: We go on a bike ride in the forest.

en cyklist.explanation: "En cyklist" means "a cyclist", someone who rides a bike. It comes from "at cykle" (to bike).

sentence.da: En **cyklist** kører på cykelstien ved siden af vejen.
sentence.en: A cyclist rides on the bike path next to the road.

et center.explanation: "Et center" means "a center" as a place or building: "et sundhedscenter" (a health center). For the middle of a city, Danes say "centrum" (downtown).

sentence.da: Der er mange butikker i det nye **center**.
sentence.en: There are many stores in the new center.

et centrum.explanation: "Et centrum" means "a center", mostly the middle of a town where the shops are. For a building like a mall, use "et center" (a shopping center).

sentence.da: Jeg bor tæt på **centrum** og cykler på arbejde.
sentence.en: I live close to the center and bike to work.

et check-in.explanation: "Et check-in" means "a check-in", the desk or moment where you register when you arrive at a hotel or an airport.

sentence.da: Ved **check-in** får du nøglen til dit værelse.
sentence.en: At check-in, you get the key to your room.

et chok.explanation: "Et chok" means "a shock", like sudden bad news. To be in shock is "at være i chok": "Han er stadig i chok" (He is still in shock).

sentence.da: Det var et **chok** at høre om ulykken.
sentence.en: It was a shock to hear about the accident.

et ciffer.explanation: "Et ciffer" means "a digit", one single symbol from 0 to 9: "25 har to cifre" (25 has two digits). A number like 100 has three.

sentence.da: Det sidste **ciffer** i koden er syv.
sentence.en: The last digit in the code is seven.

et cirkus.explanation: "Et cirkus" means "a circus", a show in a big tent with animals and performers. It can also mean a chaotic mess: "Det er et cirkus herhjemme" (It is a circus at home).

sentence.da: Vi skal i **cirkus** i aften og se dyr.
sentence.en: We are going to the circus tonight to see animals.

et citat.explanation: "Et citat" means "a quote", words taken exactly from what someone else said or wrote, and used again in a new place.

sentence.da: Hun bruger et **citat** fra bogen i sin tale.
sentence.en: She uses a quote from the book in her speech.

et computerspil.explanation: "Et computerspil" means "a computer game". It is built from computer and spil (game), and it also means games on a phone.

sentence.da: I et **computerspil** styrer man en figur på skærmen.
sentence.en: In a computer game you control a character on the screen.

et cpr-nummer.explanation: "Et CPR-nummer" means "a CPR number", the personal ID number every person living in Denmark has.

sentence.da: Jeg skriver mit **CPR-nummer** på formularen hos lægen.
sentence.en: I write my CPR number on the form at the doctor's.

et crush.explanation: "Et crush" means "a crush", a person you are romantically attracted to. Danes borrowed the English word, and use "på" (on) with it: "et crush på en kollega" (a crush on a coworker).

sentence.da: Hun rødmer, hver gang hendes **crush** smiler til hende.
sentence.en: She blushes every time her crush smiles at her.

et cv.explanation: "Et cv" means "a CV", the paper listing your work and education, which you send with an application.

sentence.da: Jeg skal opdatere mit **cv** i dag.
sentence.en: I have to update my CV today.

et cykelbud.explanation: "Et cykelbud" means "a bike courier", someone who brings food or parcels by bike. It is built from en cykel (a bike) and et bud (a messenger).

sentence.da: Et **cykelbud** kom med pizzaen på ti minutter.
sentence.en: A bike courier came with the pizza in ten minutes.

et cykelløb.explanation: "Et cykelløb" means "a bike race", a competition where riders follow a set route and the fastest wins.

sentence.da: Til et **cykelløb** vinder den, der først krydser målstregen.
sentence.en: At a bike race, the one who first crosses the finish line wins.

et cykelstativ.explanation: "Et cykelstativ" means "a bike rack", a metal stand where you park your bike. It is built from cykel (bike) and stativ (stand).

sentence.da: Jeg låser min cykel fast i et **cykelstativ**.
sentence.en: I lock my bike to a bike rack.

at dampe.explanation: "At dampe" means "to steam", to send up steam, as hot things do. It is also used for cooking in steam: "at dampe grøntsager" (to steam vegetables).

sentence.da: Den varme suppe begynder at **dampe**, når låget løftes.
sentence.en: The hot soup starts to steam when the lid is lifted.

at danne.explanation: "At danne" means "to form", to make something come into being: "at danne en regering" (to form a government). For shaping clay or dough with your hands, use "at forme" (to shape).

sentence.da: Vand kan **danne** is, når det bliver meget koldt.
sentence.en: Water can form ice when it gets very cold.

at danse.explanation: "At danse" means "to dance", to move to music alone or with a partner. To name your dance partner, use "med" (with): "Jeg danser med Anna" (I dance with Anna).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **danse** til musikken.
sentence.en: I want to dance to the music.

at date.explanation: "At date" means "to date", to see someone romantically, to get to know them better. For the day on a calendar, use "en dato" (a date on the calendar).

sentence.da: Hun vil gerne **date** en sød fyr.
sentence.en: She would like to date a nice guy.

at debattere.explanation: "At debattere" means "to debate", to talk openly about a question where people have different opinions, often in public or in the media: "Vi debatterer skolereformen" (We are debating the school reform). Among friends, people more often say "at diskutere" (to discuss).

sentence.da: Politikerne skal **debattere** loven i Folketinget i morgen.
sentence.en: The politicians are going to debate the law in Parliament tomorrow.

at definere.explanation: "At definere" means "to define", to say exactly what a word or an idea means. It is also used for goals: "at definere et mål" (to define a goal).

sentence.da: En ordbog hjælper dig med at **definere** ukendte ord.
sentence.en: A dictionary helps you define unknown words.

at dele.explanation: "At dele" means "to share", and "med" (with) names who you share with: "Jeg deler min mad med dig" (I share my food with you). It also means "to divide", as in math: "ti delt med to" (ten divided by two).

sentence.da: Vi vil **dele** en pizza.
sentence.en: We want to share a pizza.

at dele ud.explanation: "At dele ud" means "to hand out", to give something to each person in a group: "Læreren deler opgaverne ud" (The teacher hands out the assignments). It is built from dele (to share) and ud (out). Do not mix it up with "at dele" (to share), where people use the same thing together: "Vi deler en pizza" (We share a pizza).

sentence.da: Han skal **dele ud** til alle børnene.
sentence.en: He is going to hand things out to all the children.

at delegere.explanation: "At delegere" means "to delegate", to hand a task or some power to someone else to handle. To name the person who receives the task, add "til" (to): "Hun delegerer opgaven til Lars" (She delegates the task to Lars).

sentence.da: En god leder tør **delegere** ansvar til andre.
sentence.en: A good leader dares to delegate responsibility to others.

at deltage.explanation: "At deltage" means "to participate" or "to take part", and you add "i" (in) before the event: "Jeg deltager i mødet" (I am taking part in the meeting).

sentence.da: Alle kan **deltage** i kurset gratis.
sentence.en: Everyone can take part in the course for free.

at demonstrere.explanation: "At demonstrere" means "to demonstrate", to show how something works. It also means to take part in a protest: "Folk demonstrerer foran Christiansborg" (People are demonstrating in front of Christiansborg, the parliament building).

sentence.da: Hun vil **demonstrere**, hvordan maskinen virker.
sentence.en: She will demonstrate how the machine works.

at designe.explanation: "At designe" means "to design", to plan how something will look and work before it is made: "Hun designer hjemmesider" (She designs websites).

sentence.da: Arkitekten skal **designe** et nyt hus.
sentence.en: The architect is going to design a new house.

at dirigere.explanation: "At dirigere" means "to conduct" an orchestra, and also "to direct" people or traffic: "Politiet dirigerer trafikken" (The police are directing traffic). For a film, use "at instruere" (to direct a film) instead.

sentence.da: Han skal **dirigere** koret ved koncerten i aften.
sentence.en: He is going to conduct the choir at the concert tonight.

at diskutere.explanation: "At diskutere" means "to discuss". For an angry fight, use "at skændes" (to quarrel): "De skændes hele tiden" (They quarrel all the time).

sentence.da: Vi skal **diskutere** problemet med læreren.
sentence.en: We have to discuss the problem with the teacher.

at distrahere.explanation: "At distrahere" means "to distract", to take someone's attention away from what they are doing. Someone can do it on purpose: "Tyven distraherede vagten" (The thief distracted the guard).

sentence.da: Telefonen kan **distrahere** dig, når du laver lektier.
sentence.en: The phone can distract you when you do homework.
